hints.title: Calculate Pair Products
hints.text: Compute the product of all pairs (nums[i], nums[j]) with i < j and store their frequencies in a map.

hints.title: Permutations Per Pair of Pairs
hints.text: For any two disjoint pairs (a, b) and (c, d) sharing the same product, there are 8 valid tuple arrangements.

hints.title: Combinatorial Accumulation
hints.text: If a product occurs k times, it contributes 8 * (k * (k - 1) / 2) valid tuples to the total.

hints.title: Full Implementation

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing 4-tuples naively requires O(n^4) quartic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pairwise product frequency hashing reduces evaluation to O(n^2) time and space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate explains why each combination of 2 pairs yields 8 distinct tuples (2 * 2 * 2).
